_comment: Index of curify-gallery/ecommerce_ad_videos for SMM distribution (FB Groups + Kuaishou + RedNote). Drafted 2026-09-06; folder consolidated into 2026-09-01-ecommerce on 2026-09-11. FB copy in posts_fb.md, 中文 copy for BOTH 快手 and 小红书 in posts_rednote_kuaishou.md (the two Chinese channels were merged into one file 2026-09-19), all keyed by the id field below. fabric_ad added 2026-09-18. 2026-09-22: the four videos that sat loose in the folder root (matcha_drink, rotation_chair, fabric_ad, beauty_cream) moved into per-id folders like the rest, each with a `watermarked` sibling built by ecommerce_ad_videos/watermark_videos.py (house tiled -30 slant, params taken verbatim from curify-frontend/scripts/lib/watermark.cjs). model-standing.mp4 deliberately left in the root. clearance drives whether an item may go on a public feed at all -- see README.md (Clearance) and curify-studio/docs/asset-authority-distribution-inventory.md sec 3 group B.

cta.batch_line_en: We do these in batches for catalogs -- one product, a full set of ad cuts. Contact us: curify-ai.com/contact
cta.batch_line_zh: 整个产品线可以批量做 -- 一个 SKU 出一整套广告片。批量合作私信或看主页 curify-ai.com

clearance_tiers.ship: Own or unbranded output. Cleared for public feeds.
clearance_tiers.check: One unresolved question (likeness or source footage provenance). Hold until answered.
clearance_tiers.internal: Third-party trademark or character IP rendered on screen. Internal / investor decks only -- never a public feed. Matches the group-B rule in asset-authority-distribution-inventory.md.

videos.brand_on_screen: none on the product; Curify CTA card
videos.clearance_note: Own output end to end. The bag is unbranded -- ivory leather, generic gold clasp -- and derives from our own curify-fashion.png poster, itself generated. Audio is a synthesized instrumental bed plus an ElevenLabs narration track; no third-party song, no voice clone of a real person. Production notes state plainly that this is an AI campaign demonstration, NOT footage of a customer project, and the narration makes no success-rate or client claim. ⚠️ One photoreal model face -- the likeness chain is generated-from-generated (text prompt + our own poster as reference), so the exposure is lower than model_standing's, but it is the same class of open question.

videos.subject: Desert dig live-action, oil pour into a gold-rim vessel, OILIGHT wordmark-and-flame logo end card
videos.clearance_note: Two open questions: (1) OILIGHT appears to be a real third-party or client brand -- publishing it as our marketing sample needs their written OK, or the client-confidential rule applies; (2) the opening desert footage is live-action with an identifiable person, so it is either licensed stock or someone else's footage. Resolve both before use.

videos.subject: Tang-dynasty court dress try-on: bellingham_male, haaland_male, haaland_female
videos.clearance_note: ⛔ REAL, IDENTIFIABLE FOOTBALLERS. The faces are recognisably two current professional players, and one clip is a gender-swapped version of one of them. Using a named athlete's likeness in outbound marketing is a publicity-rights problem, and commercial use is the aggravating factor rather than a mitigating one -- these are among the most commercially licensed faces in sport. The gender-swap adds a separate harm: altering a real identifiable person's appearance in commercial content. Same tier as corona/starbucks/popmart: internal decks and sales calls only, never a public feed. ⚠️ Also note the on-screen TANG DYNASTY title renders doubled/ghosted in all three.
videos.unlock: Re-render the same wardrobe and choreography on SYNTHETIC identities. The craft is in the costume, lighting and the change itself, not in whose face it is -- the same one-swap unlock prompts/beauty_cream.json records for the branded case. Costs one generation each.

videos.subject: female-beat-matched, male-beat-matched -- held fashion poses cut to music accents
videos.clearance_note: ⛔ CLIENT WORK. Its own README states the deliverables are saved into client_VC_portfolio/fashion-model-09-05/ -- the client-006 line, customer_data: true, whose OOTD job is recorded client_satisfied: false. Both clips are driven by counterparty-supplied WeChat reference videos; the README describes the female clip as 'a very close reference-guided recreation of the same female character, setting and pose sequence', i.e. a recreation of someone else's creative, and the male identity comes from that same client job's model image. Publishing either as our marketing republishes a counterparty's work. Internal only.
videos.unlock: The FORMAT is ours to use -- held poses cut to measured audio accents, validated here to within one frame at 30fps. Re-run it on our own synthetic identity and our own music and it ships. What cannot travel is this character, this wardrobe and this pose sequence.
videos.craft_note: Timing validation is unusually good and worth keeping as method: cuts within 8-17ms of selected onsets, music correlation 0.991-0.993 after AAC export, zero measured offset.
